Siedlce Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Siedlce, Poland

Demolished. This second, 'old' Jewish cemetery in Siedlce was established before 1798, possibly as early as the second quarter of the 18th century, on the city's western outskirts. It remained active until around 1807, when sanitary concerns prompted establishment of a newer cemetery further from the developing city (see the Siedlce New Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history, including its role as a 1942 mass-execution site during the ghetto's liquidation). Germans completely destroyed this cemetery during WWII; Communist-era development built service buildings and apartment blocks on the grounds.
